messages.author: 052dc98fd0a6fd98
messages.subject: mesh generation hanging (fmesher64, inla.mesh.2d)
parts:
Hi there!

I am trying to create meshes (using inla.mesh.2d) in an unsupervised/automated setting and am encountering numerous situations where various (and as yet unclear) sets of mesh creation options (offset, cutoff, boundary) results in the mesh not being resolved ... indefinately. I have not been able to figure out the minimal conditions necessary to make this happen. I am wondering if anyone in the group has experienced this and if they have found a work-around? I can vary the settings manually until a solution is found but I am doing this more-or-less by guessing. As I have many thousands of such meshes to create, I am hoping for a method that does not require hand tweaking. 

Any advice would be appreciated!

Best wishes,
Jae

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh generation hanging (fmesher64, inla.mesh.2d)
parts:
Ok, thanks.
Your JPEG reveals that it's a well known issue that used to be common, but is now more rare after the code was made more robust, where the initial mesh construction gets stuck in a loop swapping between two equivalent Delaunay triangulations.  It's a difficult problem to solve completely in the internal code. It only occurs for regular input; small perturbations avoids the problem. Due to floating point arithmetic, rescaling is sometimes enough of a perturbation.

I'll see if I can use your test cases to see why the previous robustifications don't always work.

Finn

On 9 Sep 2015, at 14:53, Jae Choi <choi.j...@gmail.com> wrote:
That is helpful. 

Would there be a way to make fmesher count some (user-) defined number of comparisons and returns an error or a null solution after cross the threshold? At least, that way, I can try to catch the errors and then try different mesh parameters.
I'll likely have to add an option for that, yes, but it's not in the code now.
I suppose for now, a quick solution would be for me to discretize the data in a non-uniform/non-lattice manner.

The problem tends to occur only in the initial stage of meshing, when it builds the outer boundary layer.  Using an odd number of points (n=17 or 33 or 65 for example) may be more robust.

Finn

For my problems, it was a race condition where multiple equivalent solutions were found to be optimal. It is apparently hard to fix this at the moment.  My fix was to add a small random offset to positional data to break the geometric symmetry.

Jae

messages.author: b16a5af9e10063ea
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh generation hanging (fmesher64, inla.mesh.2d)
parts:
My problems appear to arise from the fact that my points are sampled from (an albeit large) regular grid. Once in every couple hundred replicates a particular arrangement of points sampled from this grid cannot be turned into a mesh without hanging. 

Here is my solution:

require(raster)
require(INLA)
require(R.utils)

## create random grid and sample from it - this is not my dataset so is unlikely to recreate the error
rast1<-raster()
coords2<-xyFromCell(rast1,1:ncell(rast1),spatial=T)[sample(1:ncell(rast1),20000),]

## set up error
e <- simpleError("test error")
mesh5<-NULL

### while mesh5 is not a mesh
while(!class(mesh5)[1]=="inla.mesh"){

## run mesh with time limit of 20 seconds
mesh5<-tryCatch(evalWithTimeout({inla.mesh.2d(loc= coordinates(coords2), max.edge = c(10, 100), cutoff = 0.1, offset = c(1, 25))}, timeout=20, onTimeout="warning"),error=function(e) e)
## if time limited reached tryCatch returns a simple error
if(class(mesh5)[1]=="simpleError"){

## if it fails jitter coodinates very slightly
coords2<-data.frame(x=jitter(coordinates(coords2)[,1],0.1),y=jitter(coordinates(coords2)[,2],0.1))
coordinates(coords2)<-~x+y
                   }#end of simple error if

      }## end of while

using this code you need to keep checking you running processes and manually kill any hanging fmeshers64 processes. I have written some code to identify and kill the hanging processes but it is unweidly and not annotated.

Hope this helps

Dave
